Subject: Hosted API: help clarifying geo-routing & subprocessors for DPA

Hi Marissa,

We're moving through procurement for our pilot and Legal has asked for short, public-facing language we can include in our vendor summary regarding two things: (1) how Redwood routes requests geographically (data-in-flight / processing locations, and residency guarantees where available) and (2) a plain-language explanation of how subprocessors are used and where to find the list.

They're not asking for full DPA text — just 1–2 short bullets and a one-line console help blurb your sales team can paste into our procurement packet. Can you also confirm whether the Hosted API page we sent encrypts customer data in-transit and whether customers can bring their own KMS for Dedicated/Private?

I've attached our current redlines to the DPA (bluebridge_dpa_redlines.pdf) and a procurement checklist so you can see the requested format.

Would you be able to send a draft by EOD today? We need something for the packet before the Friday exec review.

Thanks,
Elena Ross
Sr. Procurement Manager
BlueBridge Health

Subject: RE: Hosted API: help clarifying geo-routing & subprocessors for DPA

Thanks for the note and the attachments, Elena — helpful context. Looping in Laura (privacy) and Karthik (product) for technical/legal signoff.

Below are two versions you can use: a short sentence for the console/help text and a slightly expanded bullet pair for your procurement packet. If you prefer we can also provide a diagram (see attached draft) and a one-page FAQ.

--- Suggested console one-liner (concise) ---
"Redwood routes requests to nearby regions to minimize latency; we provide data residency options for supported regions and publish our subprocessors list at https://docs.redwood.ai/dpa/subprocessors."

--- Procurement bullets (slightly expanded) ---
- Geo-routing & residency: Requests are routed to a model-serving cluster in the configured region to reduce latency. For customers who require residency, we offer region-locking for supported models and retain control-plane metadata in the US/EU as requested.
- Subprocessors: Redwood uses subprocessors (cloud providers, CDN, observability tooling) to operate the service. We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors and locations at https://docs.redwood.ai/dpa/subprocessors; customers can request advance notice for added subprocessors under our DPA.

Regarding encryption and KMS: Hosted API encrypts all data in transit using TLS. Customers on Dedicated or Private can integrate with their KMS/HSM for key management. Laura and Karthik — please confirm wording is accurate and safe to publish.

I attached a quick geo-routing sketch (geo-routing-diagram.png) — feel free to use it in the packet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions (Sales) Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: geo-routing-diagram.png

Marissa — good draft. A couple of edits so the language is clear for procurement/legal reviewers: replace "retain control-plane metadata in the US/EU as requested" with "control-plane metadata is stored in the region you select; sensitive customer content may be processed outside the region for inference where necessary but we provide contractual residency options for supported models." Also clarify subprocessors are engaged on a need basis and data access is limited.

Suggested revised procurement bullets:
- Geo-routing & residency: By default, requests are routed to the nearest Redwood serving region to optimize latency. For customers requiring residency, Redwood offers region-locking for supported models and contractual guarantees about where customer content is stored and processed. Note: certain model architectures or external integrations may require fallback routing for compatibility; Redwood documents fallback behavior in the product guide.
- Subprocessors: Redwood engages subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring, and CDN partners) to run and operate the service. Subprocessor access to customer content is limited by contract and least-privilege controls; an up-to-date list is published at https://docs.redwood.ai/dpa/subprocessors and available on request.

Also: "encrypts all data in transit using TLS" is fine; add that Hosted API uses TLS 1.2+ and supports HTTP/2. For KMS, say "customers on Dedicated or Private can integrate their KMS/HSM or use Redwood-managed keys per contract."

Marissa, Karthik — if that looks good I can sign off and we can deliver final copy to Elena.

-Laura
Principal Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks, and great questions. Final answers and copy below. Mina is copied for product ops/console copy handoff.

1) Console one-liner (<= 20 words) — approved for Sales/Console use:
"Requests are routed to regional serving clusters; see subprocessors and residency options at https://docs.redwood.ai/dpa/subprocessors."

2) Subprocessors list granularity — yes. The published list includes vendor names and country-level locations; we can provide more granular region info under NDA or as part of the DPA appendix.

3) Control-plane metadata at rest — we encrypt control-plane metadata at rest using AES-256; customer content storage options vary by deployment (Hosted: encrypted at rest in supported region; Dedicated/Private: customer-managed keys available).

Procurement bullets (final):
- Geo-routing & residency: By default, requests are routed to the nearest Redwood serving region to optimize latency. For customers requiring residency, Redwood offers region-locking for supported models and contractual guarantees about where customer content is stored and processed; fallback routing behaviour is documented in the product guide.
- Subprocessors: Redwood engages subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring, and CDN partners) to operate the service. Access to customer content by subprocessors is limited by contract, least-privilege controls, and documented in our published subprocessors list (country-level locations available).

I've attached the final geo diagram (updated) and will ask Mina to push the one-liner into the Hosted API console help text and to the Sales snippet library. Laura — please let me know if you want any additional legal qualifiers in the final packet.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-minute call if BlueBridge wants to walk through the language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
